good_pawn: Bring your pawn to d5. This move hits the white pawn on e4 and fights for the middle. It is fine, but e5 is a little better. With e5 you control the middle right away. Lesson: in the start, push a middle pawn to grab the center.

Your friend pushed a pawn to e5 and grabbed space in the middle. Their bishop on g4 is pointing at your knight, but your knight is safe for now. This is a great time to make your king safe and castle. Lesson: when the middle gets busy, tuck your king away first.
Black put a pawn in the middle, just like you did. Now you can bring your knight out to f3 and aim at that e5 pawn. Get your pieces out early and fight for the middle.

You moved your pawn to d6. This guards your pawn on e5 and lets your bishop on c8 come out later. A nice move too is to castle and tuck your king away safe. Remember, protect your pawns and get your king safe early.
Move forward your pawn two steps in the middle. This opens space for your bishop and queen to come out later. Try to take the middle of the board with your pawns early.
You moved your pawn up one small step with d3. It is okay but a bit shy. Better was d4 to push two steps and grab the middle. Lesson: in the start, fight hard for the middle squares.

Good try! Your pawn moved up and now your queen checks the king. But the move Be3 was a bit better and keeps your pieces strong and safe. Lesson, before you push a pawn, make sure it does not get lost.

You moved your pawn to d5. It hits the white pawn on e4. But white can just take it with exd5, so you do not win anything. Next time try the pawn to e5 instead. It puts a strong pawn right in the middle. Lesson: at the start, try to put a pawn in the middle of the board.
Good move. Your pawn on c6 makes a small wall and keeps you safe. It also gives your queen a spot to go back home. Lesson: a quiet pawn move can make your side safe and strong.

White just played Bc4 and your student answered e6. Nice and solid! It makes a small wall and stops the white bishop from looking at your weak spot. Now your light bishop on g4 needs a friend, so think about playing pieces to safe squares and getting your king tucked away. Lesson: after a calm move, bring out your pieces and keep your king safe.
Black just pushed a pawn to f5. It now hits your pawn on g4. You can take back with your g4 pawn. Lesson: when a pawn attacks yours, you can trade it off.

Black pushed a pawn and put your king in check. Do not grab that pawn, the black rook on d4 is guarding it. Just move your king to a safe spot like g2. When you are in check, get your king safe first.
Black copied you and played a pawn to e5. Now both center pawns face off. Bring your knight out to f3 next. It will attack the black pawn on e5. Lesson, get your knights out early to help your pawns.

Black just played d6 to guard the pawn in the middle. Now bring your knight out to f3 and get ready to castle. After that you can make your king safe by castling. Lesson: bring your pieces out and keep your king safe.

Lovely opening move! Pushing your pawn to e4 takes control of the middle of the board and opens paths for your bishop and queen to come out. Next, try to bring your knights and bishops out so they can join the fight. Remember the simple rule: in the start, move your pieces toward the middle so they can do more.
Nice move. Your pawn on d3 makes a path for your other bishop to come out. It also helps guard your pawn on e4. Good idea, keep opening paths so your pieces can come out.
Good job. You moved your pawn to the middle of the board. This helps your pieces come out fast and makes you strong in the center. Lesson: start by taking the middle with a pawn.
Nice move. Your pawn d4 goes right into the middle and takes good space. This is just what the best move is, so well done. Always try to put your pawns in the middle early.

Nice move. You put your pawn in the middle and opened space for your bishop and queen to come out. Try to bring out your knights and bishops next, then make your king safe. Good chess starts by taking the middle and getting your pieces ready.
Your move d3 only pushes the pawn one small step. A nicer move is h3. It asks the black bishop to move or trade. Try to push the bishop away when it sits next to your knight.
You pushed your pawn into the middle. This is a good move. It fights for the center squares. Always try to grab the middle of the board.
Good job, you put your pawn in the middle with e5. This is a strong move and helps you fight for the center. Lesson, pawns in the middle give your pieces more space to grow.

Bring your pawn to d5 to fight for the middle. A small note: playing your bishop to b4 with check was a little better, because it bothers the white king right away and helps your pieces get out faster. Both moves are fine here. Lesson: in the opening, try to use moves that help your pieces come out fast.

Black just pushed a pawn to d5. You can take it with your pawn on c4. After cxd5 you win that pawn, so go ahead and grab it. Lesson: when they put a pawn next to yours, you can often just take it.

Black pushed the e-pawn up two squares. This opens space for black's pieces and frees the bishop on f8. Now bring your own pieces out and get ready to castle so your king is safe. Lesson: when it is calm, get your pieces out and keep your king safe.

Your pawn on c6 pushes at the white knight, which is a nice idea. But your bishop on c5 is now loose, and white can play b4 to chase it and win time. Moving your queen to e6 first was safer because it keeps your pieces protected. Lesson: before you attack, make sure your own pieces are safe.

You moved your pawn to e5. Nice work, this is a great move. Now both your pawns sit in the middle. Next bring your knight out to a good spot. Lesson, put your pawns in the middle early.
Good job. You moved your pawn to e4. It steps into the middle and frees your bishop and queen. Remember, taking the middle early is a strong way to start.

Good job. You put a pawn in the middle next to your other pawn. Now you have two strong pawns in the center. They help your other pieces come out later. Lesson is simple, try to put pawns in the middle early.

Black just played d5 and now after some moves it's White to move with e5 as the move. Let me write the caption.

Your pawn moves up and pushes the black knight away from f6. That is a good idea because it takes space. After this your knight on f3 and bishops have more room to work. Lesson: pushing a pawn to attack a piece can win you space and time.
Play e4 to start. It puts a pawn in the middle and opens lines for your pieces. Good job. Lesson: start by taking the middle of the board.

Good move. You push your pawn to d4 and grab space in the middle. That is nice. Next time try moving your knight to f3 first to get a piece out fast. Lesson: bring your pieces out early and take the middle.
Good job. You moved your pawn to the middle of the board. This helps your pieces come out and makes more space. The middle is a great place to start, so play there early.
Nice move. Your pawn on d3 now hits the black pawn on e4. This may win that pawn or open lines for your other pieces. Lesson: use your pawns to push at the enemy and grab space.

The other player moved their pawn to e5. Now both center pawns face each other, which is fair and normal. It is your turn, so bring your knight out to f3. Lesson: in the start, bring your pieces out to good spots early.

You moved your pawn to d6. That is a small, slow step. It is better to push the pawn to d5. That pawn goes to the middle and hits the white pawn right away. Lesson: try to push a pawn into the middle early to fight for space.
You moved your pawn to c5. A better move was to bring your knight out to c6. Your knight is sitting at home and needs to join the game. Lesson: bring your pieces out before you push more pawns.
Black just pushed a pawn to c4. That pawn now attacks your bishop on d3. Move your bishop to a safe spot, like c2 or e2. Lesson: when your piece is attacked, move it to safety.
opp_trade: White just captured on d5 with the pawn. You now have a pawn in the middle on d5, which is nice. Black will likely take it back soon, so be ready. Lesson: trading is fine, but try to keep a strong pawn in the middle when you can.

Nice and steady. You take the black knight on d4. This is a fair trade and a fine move. Just keep an eye on the black bishop on g4. Lesson: a fair trade is okay, but always look at your opponent's pieces first.
Take the piece on e2 with your queen, not your rook. The queen is better here because next you can win a free pawn on e5.
You took the pawn in the middle. That is a fair trade because black just takes back. This move is fine and loses almost nothing. Lesson, swapping pawns is okay when both sides give and get the same.
You take a piece, and Black takes one right back. It is a fair, even trade — a piece for a piece, which is fine when nothing goes wrong.

You took a knight in the middle with your knight. The black pawn will take back, so this is a fair trade. That is okay here, nothing is lost. Lesson is simple, swapping pieces evenly is fine when it does not hurt you.

Their king walked out to f7 to grab your bishop. Now their king is stuck in the open with no cover. Bring your pieces toward it and look for a way to attack. The lesson is simple: a king out in the open is weak, so go after it.
Good job. Your pawn takes the black bishop. The knight takes back, but you gave a small pawn and won a big piece. When a pawn can grab a bigger piece, take it.
The other player took your knight on d5. Take it back with your pawn from e4. Lesson: when you take a piece back, see if your pawn hits something else too.
The other player took your rook with their bishop. Take the bishop back now with your f pawn (fxg3). Do not leave it there for free. When someone takes your piece, take one right back.
You took the black pawn on d5. That is a good and safe move. Black will likely take back with the queen. The lesson is simple — when you can win a pawn safely, take it.

Your knight check trades pieces, but it gives up your good bishop on c4 for not much. A better move was g4, which goes after the black bishop and can win it. Lesson: before you trade, look for a move that wins a piece first.

Black's knight jumped to f3 and put your king in check. You took that knight with your queen, which was a good, safe choice. The knight was guarded by the black queen, so this just trades pieces fairly. Lesson: when your king is in check, get it safe right away.
Your pawn grabbed a free black piece because nothing was guarding it. Always look for a piece you can take for free.
You took the black pawn on g4 with your pawn. Black can take it back with the pawn on h5, so it is a fair trade. This is fine and keeps the game even. Lesson: trading one pawn for one pawn is okay.

Good job, you take the bishop and check the king at the same time. Black must stop the check first, so they cannot do what they want. Lesson, when you can grab a piece and give check together, that is a strong move.
Good job, you won a free piece! But your king moved out a little, so bring it back to a safe spot soon.
Your rook takes the piece on f2. The black bishop will take your rook and check your king, then your king takes the bishop, so you stay ahead — a trade is good when you win more than you give.

You took the bishop on e6, but it is not free. Black just takes back with the queen, so you traded away your good bishop. A better move was Nf3, to bring your sleepy knight into the game. Lesson: get all your pieces out and playing before you trade them.

You take the black rook on d6 with your rook. Black takes back with the queen, so it is a fair, even trade. After that, keep an eye on the black knight on f4 sitting near your king. Lesson: swapping equal pieces is fine when the game is even.
Your friend just took a pawn on e4. You can take it right back by playing dxe4, so you are even again. The lesson is simple: when they take something, take it back.
Good job. You took a free pawn that nothing was guarding, so it was safe. When a pawn has no helper, you can grab it.
You take the black rook with your queen, and it gives check at the same time. No black piece was guarding that rook, so you win it for free. Lesson: always look around for a free piece you can grab.
Nice job! You took a free pawn that no black piece was guarding. When a piece is free and safe to grab, take it.

Your opponent took your rook in the corner with the bishop. But now that bishop is stuck in the corner with few safe squares. Bring a piece over and try to catch it. Lesson, grabbing a piece in the corner can leave it trapped.
Your opponent's bishop now attacks your rook. Move your rook to g1 so it is safe and it can attack that bishop too. Lesson: when a piece is in danger, move it to a safe spot.
Your friend just took one of your pawns with the bishop. Your knight can take that bishop back, but a black knight guards it, so it is a fair trade and not a free piece.
The black bishop took a pawn and checks your king. You must answer the check right now. Move your king to a safe spot. Lesson: when your king is in check, getting safe comes first.
Your queen took a piece for free because it was not guarded, so it is now lost. Lesson: always guard your pieces so they can not be grabbed for free.
Your bishop just got taken. No one was guarding it, so it was a free piece for them. Try to keep each of your pieces safe, with a friend close by to guard it.

The other player took your knight and gave check. You cannot grab the queen back, because their rook guards it. So move your king to a safe square. Lesson: always keep your pieces guarded, and watch out for the enemy queen.

Nice spot! Your knight can attack their king and their rook at the same time, so the king must move to get safe and then your knight takes the free rook. Lesson: a knight can hit two things at once, so always look for that double attack.
Your opponent took one of your pieces, but that is okay, so do not worry. Now bring your other pieces out and keep your king safe.
The other player just took one of your pieces. Take it right back so the pieces stay even, and always look to recapture.

Black took your rook on f8. You cannot win it back right now, so stay calm. Look at your strong knight on d5 in the middle and find a good move for it. Lesson: when something goes wrong, do not panic and just play your best move.
Your opponent took your pawn on d4. You can take it back. Move your rook to d4 and win the pawn back. Lesson: when they take a pawn, look to take one right back.
Black just took your pawn on d4. You can take it right back. Move your pawn from e3 to d4 and you are even again. The lesson is simple, when they take a pawn, take it back.
Good job! You took a free piece that nothing was guarding. When the other side leaves a piece open, grab it.
Nice move. You took a free pawn that nothing was guarding, so now you are up one pawn. Lesson: when a piece is not guarded, you can take it for free.
Good job. You found a free piece you could take, because nothing was guarding it. The lesson is simple, always look for a piece you can take for free.
Great move. Your queen takes the black queen on c5. It is free because the black pawn on c7 blocks the black rook. Always look for a free piece you can grab.
You took the black knight on d5. But black just takes it back with the c6 pawn. So it is only a swap, not a free piece. Lesson, before you trade, look around for an even better move first.

Pieces are even now after you take back. Take with your bishop, like fxg4, to bring it out and aim at the board. After that, get your king safe soon. Lesson: when you trade, take back so you do not lose a piece.

Nice work, you took a free pawn with your queen. Black did not guard it, so it was safe to grab. Now keep your queen safe and bring out your other pieces. Lesson, when a pawn is free and safe, you can take it.
That is a good move, you win a piece. Always look for pieces you can grab for free.

Your rook takes the black rook and gives check. The black king can just take your rook back, so it is only a trade. It is okay but not the best move you had. Lesson: before you swap pieces, look for an even better move first.
Your move wins a free pawn and gives check at the same time. The black king must move out of the way. Lesson: always look for a safe check that also grabs a free pawn.
You grabbed a free piece that no one was guarding, and that is a big win for you. Remember this: always look around for a free piece you can take.
You won a bigger piece and lost only a small pawn. Lesson: it is a good trade to give a small pawn and win a bigger piece.

Your bishop captures on f3. The black rook can take your bishop and check your king, but your king just takes that rook right back. You give a small piece and win a bigger one. Lesson: a trade is good when you get more than you give.
You take back the pawn on d4 with your c3 pawn. This keeps the pawns even, which is good. The lesson is simple: when they take a pawn, take one right back.

Great job, you played Qxf7 and it is checkmate! Your queen takes the pawn next to the king, and your bishop on c4 guards your queen so the king cannot take back. The king has no safe square to run to, so the game is won. Lesson: when your queen and bishop both aim at the same square near the king, you can win the game right there.
Good job, you took a free piece with your queen, and it was safe to grab because your king is tucked away in the corner. Lesson, when a piece is free and safe to take, grab it.
Your opponent took your bishop. You can take their piece right back. Lesson: when they take your piece, take theirs right back.
Your bishop is being attacked, but one of your own pieces is already guarding it, so the bishop is safe. Lesson: when something attacks your piece, first check if it is already guarded.
Black's knight just took your queen. Next time, look at where the enemy pieces can jump so your big pieces stay safe.
Black just took your rook on b6. But you can take that black rook right back. Move your rook from b1 up to b6 and grab it. When someone takes your piece, look to take one back.

Black just took one of your pawns far away on the side. That pawn is gone, but your rook, knight, and bishop are all deep near the black king, so keep playing over there — losing one small pawn is okay when your pieces are this strong.
Your friend took your pawn on d4. Just take it back with your queen, so move it to d4. Now you have a strong pawn in the middle. Lesson: when they take a piece, take one back so things stay even.

Black just took your bishop on c6. You can take right back with your queen, Qxc6, and this also gives a check. Take a quiet moment to play it, then your king is happy and the trade is fair. Lesson: when they take a piece, look for a good way to take one back.
When they take one of your pieces, you can take one of theirs back. That keeps things even and you are fine.

Their queen is attacking your queen, so you must act now. Take their queen with your queen — their rook will take back, and that is a fair swap. Lesson: when your queen is in danger, trading it for their queen is a safe plan.
The other player took your queen on a7. Good news, you can take their queen back. Move your rook from a1 to a7 and grab it. Lesson: when they take a piece, look for a way to take right back.

Your friend just took your pawn on b4. You can take it right back with your queen on a4. Watch out, their queen on c5 guards that square, so trading queens is the likely result. Lesson: when they grab a pawn, look for a way to win it back.
Your opponent took your pawn on e3. Good news, you can win that pawn right back. Just take the pawn on e3 and stay even. Lesson, when someone grabs a pawn, look for a way to take it back.

The other player just took one of your knights with a pawn. That is okay, because you still have more pieces than they do. Now move your knight to d5. It bothers their queen and keeps you on top. Lesson: when you have more pieces, use them and keep your king safe.
Move your queen to c7 and give check. This trades the queens off, and you are still way ahead — when you are winning, trading pieces makes the win easier.
White just played cxb4 and took the pawn. Good, you won a free pawn and your bishops now have open lines to attack. Lesson: when your opponent gives you a free pawn, it is okay to take it.

You moved your pawn to c4. It hits the black queen on d5. Now the queen has to run away. When you attack the queen with a pawn, it must move, and you get a free turn to play.

White plays the pawn to e4. This move puts a pawn in the middle of the board. It also opens lines so your bishop and queen can come out. Lesson: start by moving a center pawn to take space and free your pieces.

Good push. Your pawn goes to the middle and bumps black's pawn on e5. This grabs space and opens lines for your pieces. Remember, pawns in the middle make your game strong.

Black played a pawn to e5. Now both your middle pawns stand face to face. It is your turn, so bring a knight out to a good spot. A nice move is your knight from g1 to f3. Lesson: in the opening, get your pieces out fast and make your king safe.
Black just moved a pawn to d6. This is a slow and shy move, so you have more time. Bring out your pieces and get ready to make your king safe. Lesson: in the start, get your pieces out fast.

Black pushed a pawn to e4. It is hitting your pawn on d3. Take it back with your d-pawn. After you take, your pawn attacks the black queen, so she must run away and you win time. Lesson: when a pawn attacks you, look to take it and chase a big piece.
Good job playing the pawn to e4. It grabs space right in the middle of the board. It also opens a path for your bishop and queen to come out later. Lesson: start the game by moving a center pawn.
You moved your pawn up one small step. Now your bishop has a path to come out and play. This is a calm, safe move. Lesson: open a little path so your sleeping pieces can join the game.
You moved your pawn to c4. It hits the black rook on d5. Now that rook must run away. A small pawn can push a big piece back, so use your pawns to chase enemy pieces.
Your pawn move to f3 is calm and safe. It helps your other pawns hold together and keeps your king cozy. This was a fine choice, only a tiny bit slow. Remember, small safe moves keep your king happy.

Your pawn moved to c5 and attacks the bishop on d6. But moving your rook to h1 was a better idea here. That rook gets a clear open line to do work. Lesson: put your rooks on open lines where they can move freely.
You moved your pawn to e4. This is a great first move. It grabs space in the middle and opens paths for your bishop and queen. Lesson, in the start try to put a pawn in the middle.
Good calm move. Your pawn on d3 guards your pawn on e4. It also opens a path so your bishop on c1 can come out later. Lesson: a quiet move that helps your other pieces is a good move.

You played c3 to get ready to push a pawn. It is okay but a little slow. A better move is to bring your knight out with Nf3. That gets a piece into the game and helps your king get safe. Lesson is to bring your knights and bishops out early.
You pushed your pawn up the board. This is a good and safe move. It does not lose anything. Lesson: a calm, safe move is a good move.

You pushed your pawn up to e6. It moves closer to making a new queen. This move is fine and loses almost nothing. Just keep an eye on your king up there. Lesson: a pawn that nears the end is strong, so push it ahead.

Black just moved a pawn to e5. Now both center pawns face each other. Your turn to grow your army. Bring out a knight to f3 or your bishop to a good spot. Lesson — in the opening, get your pieces out fast and into the game.

Black moved a pawn to e5 to meet your pawn in the middle. Now it is your turn, so bring out a piece. A good idea is to move your knight from g1 to f3. Lesson: take your pieces out early and grab the middle.

Your opponent pushed a pawn to f5. This move is not safe and helps you. Push your own pawn to d4 and fight hard in the middle. The big lesson is simple, when the other player makes a loose move, hit back fast in the center.

Your knight and bishop are both out, and your king is safe. That is great work. Now it is black's turn to move, so just watch what they do. Keep your pieces ready and look after the middle of the board. Lesson: bring your pieces out early and tuck your king away safe.

Black pushed the pawn to d5 to block your bishop. Your bishop can grab that pawn, but the knight on f6 guards it. So do not take, or you swap a bishop for one pawn. Always check who guards a piece before you take it.
Your friend put a pawn in the middle too, just like you. Now bring a knight out to attack that pawn on e5. Try Ng1 to f3. Lesson: take your pieces out early and aim at the middle.

Your friend moved a pawn to d6, but it blocks their own bishop. This is a slow move, so now you can grab the middle. Push your pawn to d4 and get more pieces out fast. Lesson: when your friend plays slow, take the middle and bring your pieces out.

You pushed your c-pawn up to c5. This lets the fight for the middle stop too soon. It is better to bring your pieces out first and keep your pawns close together. Lesson: get your knights and bishops out before you push a pawn far ahead.

You moved your pawn to c4. This is a good start. It helps you grab space on one side of the board. Soon bring your knights and bishops out to play. Lesson: in the start, get your pieces out and make your king safe.

White moved the pawn to e4. This is a great first move. It puts a pawn in the middle of the board. It also opens lines for your bishop and queen to come out later. Lesson: starting in the middle of the board is a strong way to begin.

White already castled and the king is safe. Black just played c3, poking at your pawn on b2. You can take that pawn with b2 times c3 and win a free pawn. Lesson: when a small pawn comes too far, take it for free.

Black just played the pawn to e6. This keeps the black bishop on d5 safe. Now it is your turn, so look for a good plan. Try to move your rooks to open lines and keep your king safe. Lesson: when nothing is free, make your pieces better one by one.
The other player pushed a pawn to e5. That pawn now hits your queen on f4. Move your queen to a safe spot right away. Lesson: when a small pawn attacks your queen, move the queen away fast.
Black copied your move and put a pawn in the middle too. Now bring a knight out, like the one on g1 to f3. This helps you get ready to attack. Lesson: in the start, bring your pieces out fast.
Black pushed the pawn to d5. That pawn now attacks your knight on e4. Move the knight to a safe square before it is lost. Lesson: when a pawn attacks your piece, move it away to stay safe.

White just moved the knight to d4. Black played pawn to c5. This pawn attacks your knight on d4. Move your knight to a safe square now, like b3. When a pawn attacks your piece, just move it away to safety.
Black pushed a pawn to e4. It is now hitting your knight on f3. Move your knight to a safe square, like e5 or d4. Lesson: when a pawn attacks your piece, move it to safety.
Nice move! You pushed your pawn to the middle of the board. This opens space for your bishop and queen to come out. Good lesson, grab the center early with a pawn.

White's bishop moves out and waits. The opponent played c3 not a real threat. Just bring your knight out with Nf3 to attack the e5 pawn. Lesson: in the opening, bring your knights and bishops out fast.

The other player brought a knight out to c6. Now it is your turn to move. Bring your own pieces out and make your king safe. The lesson is simple: get your pieces out fast and tuck your king away early.
You brought your knight out to f6. That is okay, but Nc6 was a little better — bring your pieces out where they help and stay safe.

White just brought out your knight to f3. That is a good move. It guards your pawn and gets a piece into play. Black answered by bringing out their knight to c6. Nothing is in danger right now. Keep bringing out your knights and bishops, and get your king safe soon. Lesson: in the start, bring out your pieces and do not move the same one again and again.
Knight to f6 brings your knight out and aims at the e4 pawn. Good move! Always bring your pieces out early so they can help you.

You moved your knight out to g4. It does not win anything there, and a pawn can soon chase it back. Castling was better because it makes your king safe and brings your rook into the game. Lesson, make your king safe first, before you go hunting.

White just played Qxf2. That is a mistake. It gives away your queen for a knight. Better was Kxf2, your king takes the free knight and stays safe. Remember, before you grab a piece, check if your king can take it safely first.

Your knight grabbed the pawn and gives check. But this is not good. The white king just steps to g2 and your knight gets trapped and lost. A better move was to move your queen to d3 and trade queens. Lesson, before you grab a pawn, check that your piece can get back home safe.

You moved your pawn to c6. This move is a little slow and helps you less. It was better to move your queen back to d1. From d1 your queen stays busy and ready to help. Lesson: in a sharp spot, keep your queen active instead of making small pawn moves.
This pawn move makes your king a little less safe. Lesson: when things are quiet, move a piece to a good spot instead of pushing a pawn near your king.

Your knight gives a check, but this check does not help you. The king just steps away and you are worse. Better was to put your knight in the middle on e5, a strong safe spot. Only give a check when it really helps you.

You moved your pawn to e7, but this lets black win right away. After this, black plays the queen to h1 and your king is in checkmate. A much better move was your queen to d3 with check, which keeps you safe and busy. Lesson: before you move, always check if your own king can be caught.

Black pushed a pawn to d5 in the middle. You can take it with your pawn on e4. Play exd5 and you will be a little better. Lesson: when a pawn moves next to yours, you can take it.

White brings the bishop out and aims at f7 near your king. Now your move c5 is a small slip. Better is to move your knight to f5 and keep things calm. Try to keep your king safe before you grab space.

You took the pawn on f5, but this gives away your strong pawn in the middle. It was better to play d4 and push your pawns in the center. Try to keep your pawns in the middle of the board strong.

White just castled. Your king is now safe in the corner. That is good. But d4 was even better here. It hits the middle and opens lines for your pieces. Remember, in the start try to grab the middle of the board.

Black moved the bishop out to c5. You can push your pawn to d4 and hit that bishop. The bishop must run away, and you get more space for free. Lesson: when a pawn can chase a piece, push it and gain room.

White just castled their king to safety, good job! Now your king sits in the corner away from the middle. Try to bring out your other pieces too so they can help. Lesson: make your king safe early, then get your pieces ready to play.

Your opponent moved their bishop to e6. That was not their best move. Now you can take a free pawn with b6 takes a7. This pawn is now very close to becoming a queen, so guard it and push it. Lesson: when a pawn gets near the end of the board, help it move forward.

Your king moved to b3. Now it attacks the black rook on a2. That rook has no help, so it must run away. Lesson: when few pieces are left, your king can fight too.

You moved your king up to c4. This keeps your king near your pawn and helps guard it. Your king is a strong helper now that the board is empty. Lesson, in the endgame bring your king out to help your pawn move up.
Your queen came out early to f4. Other pieces can chase her away and you lose time. Try to bring out your knights and rooks first. Lesson: move your small pieces out before your big queen.

Your opponent moved their knight back to d7. This is a bit slow for them. Use this time to bring out your other pieces and grab more space in the middle. Lesson: when the other side plays slow, get your pieces ready and take more room.
Black's bishop on c6 now attacks your rook on b7. Your rook is not safe there, so move it away to a good square. Lesson: when a piece is attacked, move it to safety before you do anything else.

Black moved the bishop back to keep it safe from your rook. You are doing well here. Your knight sits strong in the middle of the board. Keep your pieces active and look for your next good move. Lesson — a knight in the middle is a strong knight.

Your opponent moved the dark bishop to d2. It does not really help them, so you are doing well. Now move your bishop to f6 and keep up the pressure. Lesson: when your opponent makes a weak move, stay calm and keep playing your good plan.

The black king moved away to f8. Your pieces are all close to his king. Keep them working together and look for a strong move that keeps his king stuck. Lesson: when many of your pieces point at the enemy king, keep up the attack.

Black moved the king away to d7. Now your queen on h8 and your bishop on h6 both hit the bishop on f8. Only the black queen guards it, so take f8 and win a piece. Lesson: when a piece loses its guard, take it.
Your opponent moved their king to e7. This is not a real threat, so stay calm. Look for your own good moves now. Lesson: when the other king just walks, check your pieces and keep your king safe.
The other player moved their king out to e6. Your rook on a7 is strong and active. Keep your rooks busy and look for free pawns to grab. Lesson: active rooks win endings, so let them attack.

Your opponent moved the bishop to the side, all the way to a4. This is not scary for you, so stay calm. Your rook on b7 is strong and points at the black pawn on f7. Keep your rooks busy on the open lines and try to win a pawn. Lesson: put your rooks where they can see far and do work.

Black put the king next to your knight on c7. But you have a strong reply. Move your knight to e6. This checks the king and also hits the black queen. The king must move away. Then you grab the queen for free. Lesson: when you give a check, look if it hits another piece too.

Black put the queen right next to your king. Your king cannot move away, and it cannot take the queen because a pawn guards it. This is checkmate, so the game is over. Next time, make your king safe early by moving it to the corner.
opp_luft: You played h3 to make a little air for your king. But this is a slow move and wastes a turn. It is better to bring a piece out or push in the middle. Remember, early in the game move your pieces out fast, not small pawn moves.
You moved your h-pawn up one square. That is okay, you only lost a tiny bit. You could also take the black pawn on g4 with your pawn. Try to keep some pawns near your king so he stays safe.

You pushed your pawn to h3. It pokes the black bishop on g4. Now the bishop must take your knight or step back. Either way you make the other player choose. Lesson: a small pawn push can ask a piece to move.
Your pawn goes to h3 and pokes the black knight on g4. Now that knight has to run away, and that is good for you. Lesson: a small pawn push can chase an enemy piece back.

White just moved a pawn next to your king to make a small safe spot. This is fine and stops back row tricks. Now you can get back to your own plan. Lesson: a quiet little pawn move can keep your king safe.
opp_queen_safety: Your queen is deep in their side on d7. They just moved their queen to attack it. You can swap queens by taking on e7, or move your queen to a safe spot. When a piece is in danger, trade it or move it away.
Black moved the queen to d7. Now look at the pawn on a7. No black piece guards it. Your queen on b7 can take it for free with Qxa7. Lesson, when a pawn has no guard, grab it.
Black moved the queen to d7. Your knight on f7 is safe, because your bishop guards it. So jump the knight to h8 and win the rook in the corner. Lesson: when your piece is safe, take the free rook.
Black moved the queen to d7. Your knight sits far away in the corner on h8. Bring it back out to a safe square. Lesson, a piece stuck in the corner does almost nothing.

Bring your queen back to d1, your queen is safe now. The black knight on b4 is eyeing your pieces, so chase it away with a3 next. Lesson: a queen that comes out too early can get chased around, so bring out your small pieces first.
Their queen moved back to c8. Now it guards their rook deep on c2. Keep your king safe and try to swap off that rook. Lesson, if a piece bothers you, trade it away.

Black moved the queen to e7. Now it is your turn. Bring your sleeping pieces out and get your king safe by castling. Try to win back one of those two black pawns sitting in the middle. The lesson is simple, get your pieces out early and keep your king safe.
good_rook_activity: Your rook moved up to h3 and that is a fine move. Now it can slide sideways and join the attack on the black king at f7. Keep playing for ways to bring your rook to a busy spot. Lesson: a rook is happy when it has open lines to move along.
Good job, this move gives a check. Your rook on f3 hits the black king on f7. Now the king must move out of the way. Lesson, a check makes your enemy do what you want.

Your rook moves to g3 and gives a check. The king must move away. But the quiet move Qe3 was a bit better here, because your queen helps more from there. Lesson, a check is not always the best move, so look for strong quiet moves too.

Black moved their rook to d5, right in the middle. That is a good, active spot for it. Now bring your own pieces out, like your sleeping bishop on c1. Lesson, get all your pieces into the game so they can help.
Your rook slides over to f5. This guards your pawn on g5, which the white bishop was about to take. Nice job, now your pawn is safe. Lesson: when a piece is in danger, look for a way to protect it.
Nice move. Your rook slides over to an open line. Now it has more room to act later. A rook is happy on a line with no pawns in the way.
Black moved the rook to d4. Now it hits your pawn on d3, and that pawn has no helper. Move your rook to d1 to guard it. Lesson: when one of your pieces is attacked, give it a guard.

You moved your rook to c1. A better move was to push your h pawn up one step. That gives your king some air and keeps it safe. After your rook move, the black queen can grab your pawn on a7. Always make your king safe first, then do the rest.

Nice move! Your rook goes to b4 and checks the black king. The king must run or block right away. This was a great choice and the best one too. Lesson: a check makes your opponent stop and deal with your move first.
Your rook went to d7 to help your king. But moving your king to c8 was safer. It steps away from the danger near it. Lesson: when things feel scary, make your king safe first.
Nice move. You put your rook on the open line. Now your rook points down at white's pieces and king. This is a strong spot for it. Lesson: put your rook on an open line where it can see far.

Your opponent moved their rook back to e7. It is safe there and does not threaten anything. You are doing fine, so keep your pieces active and push your pawns. When few pieces are left, walk your king out to help.

Black moved the rook to e6. Now it points at your knight on e5. But your knight is safe, because your other knight on d3 guards it. Lesson: keep your pieces guarding each other, so nothing is left alone.
Your rook drops down to g1, which is okay. But pushing the h-pawn with h4 was a bit better. That pawn can run down and become a new queen. Lesson: when a pawn can race to the end, push it.

Black's rook now sits next to your knight on f4. Do not worry, your other knight on g6 keeps it safe. If the rook takes it, just take back. The lesson is simple: a piece is safe when a friend guards it.
Your rook went all the way to g1. A better spot was g3, closer to the action. From g3 your rook can grab the pawn on a3 soon and stay busy. Try to keep your rook active and near the fight.

The black rook moved next to your king and gives check. You must answer it right now. Just move your king to a safe square away from the rook. Lesson: when your king is in check, get it to safety first.

The black rook slid over and now aims at your a3 pawn. That pawn is not guarded, so you must save it now. Bring your king or knight over to protect it. Lesson: always check what the enemy piece is attacking, and guard it.
Your rook moved over to f1. This helps keep your f2 pawn safe. Nice and steady play. Lesson: always guard your weak pawns.

Nice move, your rook on b7 now attacks the black bishop on d7. The black king guards it, so you cannot win it for free yet, but your rook is very strong on this row. Lesson: a rook is powerful when it sits deep in the other side's row.

Good job. You move your rook to b4. Now both your rooks watch the b file. They stop the black pawn on b2 from making a new queen. Two rooks working together are very strong. Lesson: put your rooks on the same line to help each other.
good_luft: Your h6 move makes a small hole for your king but loses a little time. A better move was Kh8, just tucking your king safe in the corner first. Try to make your king fully safe before you push pawns near it.
Your pawn went to h6. It pokes the white bishop and asks it to move away. This is a fine and safe move. Lesson, a small pawn push can chase a big piece back.

Your move h3 just pushes a pawn next to your king. A better try was Rc1, which slides your rook onto the open line where it can do more. Remember, rooks are happy on open lines with no pawns in the way.
good_rook_open_file: Nice move. Your rook slides over to d6. Now it stands on a clear lane with no pawns blocking it. It also points at the other side of the board. Good job — try to put your rooks on open lines where they can see far.
Nice move, your rook now attacks the white knight on g6. This also keeps your rook active and helps your king stay safe. Lesson: put your rook where it does two good jobs at once.

Nice move. Your rook now attacks the black queen, so she must run away. This gives you time to keep your king safe and stay calm. Remember, when you push a strong piece at the enemy queen, you make her waste a turn moving.
Your rook jumps to c2 and goes after the b2 pawn. That is a fine idea, but a tiny bit better was g6 to give your king more air first. Grabbing a pawn is nice, but a safe king matters even more.

The black rook jumped back to g1, far from the fight. That gives you time, so keep your pieces working together. A good idea is to move your knight to e1 and stay safe. Remember, when your opponent moves away, use the spare time to make your side strong.

Black moved the rook to check your king. You must get out of check first. Move your king to a safe square. Then keep pushing your extra pawn to make a new queen. Lesson is simple, when you are in check, make your king safe before anything else.

The black rook went far away to a8. This gives you time to push your b pawn up the board. Keep your king and knight close to guard it. Remember, when the other rook is far away, march your pawn forward.

Good job, your rook went deep into black's side. That is a strong and active spot. The move Rc7 was just a tiny bit better, but yours is almost as good. Lesson, your rook is happy when it goes far up the board.

Nice move. Your rook went to c1. Now it points right at the black rook on c2. The black rook is not safe there, so black must move it or lose it. Lesson: put your rooks on open lines so they can attack.
White just moved the rook to c1. This brings your rook over to a good open line. It is a fine move and keeps your rook active. Lesson: put your rooks on open lines where they can do the most.

Nice move. Your rook on c4 now looks at the black pawn on b4. That pawn is guarded by the black rook, so it is not free yet. Still, your rook is active and doing real work. Lesson: put your rooks where they can attack things.
good_capture_free: Your move grabbed something for free because nothing was guarding it, so it was safe and good. Lesson — when a piece has no guard, you can take it for free.

Nice job taking the rook in the corner with your knight. That move is okay, but the knight can get stuck way over there. A little better was to bring your knight back to the middle on e5, where it is strong and safe. Lesson: winning a piece is good, but always check that your piece can get back out and stay safe.
Good job. Watch out for the pawn going to g3 — your queen will need a safe spot to step back. Lesson: when a piece is free and safe to take, take it.
Your friend just took one of your pawns for free because no other piece was guarding it. Next time, keep each pawn safe by putting another piece next to it.
Your opponent just took your pawn on c4. Do not panic, you can win this pawn back later. For now, bring your pieces out and fight for the middle. Remember, do not rush to grab a pawn back right away.
Black took a pawn from you. Don't worry—move your bishop to e5 and take a pawn back. Lesson: when they take one pawn, look for a way to take one back.
Nice job. You win a free pawn with no danger. Lesson — when a pawn is free and safe to take, grab it.
You won the game. It is checkmate and the black king has no safe square left. Lesson, look for moves that check the king so it has no escape.
Your king takes a free piece. It was not guarded, so you win it for free. Lesson: when a piece is not guarded, take it.
Nice job, your knight won a big black piece for free. Now bring it back to safety soon so black cannot trap it in the corner.
opp_rook_open_file: Black moved the rook next to the queen. They want to give checks and bother your king. Watch out, and keep a safe escape square for your king. Lesson: when they aim at your king, make it safe first.

You moved your rook onto the empty line. Now it looks straight up at the black queen. This move is okay, but a small bit better was possible. Remember this: rooks are happy on empty lines where nothing blocks them.
You moved your rook over to the e file. This lines it up with the black pieces in the middle. It was a fine move, just a little slow. Remember to put your rooks on open lines where they can do more.

You moved your rook to e2, and your queen on a6 keeps it safe. Now you face the black rook and ask to trade. If black takes your rook, your queen just takes back. When the enemy rook is busy and strong, swap it off.

You move your rook to d8 and give a check. The black king must run to h7. This is fine, but watch out — black's rook and knight sit close to your king. A check is only good when it helps your plan, so keep your king safe too.

Black moved a rook to b8. Now it points right at your rook on b6. Your rook on b6 has no friend guarding it. So move your rook away to a safe square first. Lesson: when a piece is attacked and not guarded, move it to safety.

Black moved the rook over to c8. This rook now looks down an open line. Stay calm and keep all your pieces safe. Check if any of your pieces can be taken before you move. Lesson: before each move, look at what your opponent wants to do.
